name: limit_engraved_text_that_exits_the_face
why: THE REASON THIS OPERATION EXISTS THIS WAY. An inscription that sticks out of the face is cut away IN SILENCE: the feature is born green, it is called Taglio-Estrusione1, and the part holds «PRO» instead of «PROVA». No error anywhere, and on a serial number there is nothing to notice it from by looking at the tree.
_why_measured_and_not_deduced: «PROVA» 10 mm high, engraved 2 mm, on a 100x100 square: anchored at the centre it removes 230.70 mm3, anchored at (30, 10) it removes 111.20. Half. The volume is the only place where the difference shows, and nobody looks at it.
_why_the_width_is_not_computed: The width of an inscription cannot be derived from the string: it depends on the drawing of the glyphs. «PROVA» 10 mm high in Century Gothic is 47.05 mm wide -- a number that can only be MEASURED, by reading the outlines that SOLIDWORKS built. That is why the check sits after the sketch text and before the cut: it is the only moment when the inscription exists and the part is not yet ruined.

expect.tolerance_why: it is the same sum of 56 curved outlines as in the green case
the width comes from the drawing of the glyphs, and below a tenth of a millimetre it is not a number to lean on

expect.why: AFTER THE REFUSAL THE SAME INSCRIPTION, MOVED, GOES THROUGH AND REMOVES ALL THE 230.70 mm3. It is the half that counts: without it, the refusal above would be indistinguishable from an operation that does not work, and the sketch left lying around by the refused step would show up here -- because the count would come out double.
